decisions.id: Summary - step 3 planned now, phase tasks filed after the checkpoint
decisions.summary: Only T01-T06 (step 3) are planned; each phase task is filed with its own plan section and plan review after the GM approves the target.
decisions.why: FR-002 and the design's step 3 put the GM's target before any phase is rebuilt; deferring the phases' planning past that point is stricter, not narrower. FR-003's one-task-per-phase is still owed and the Project Structure names it.

decisions.id: D1 - derivation from the contract alone
decisions.summary: Each stage's derivation is the template filled from its docstring, plan fields read, manifest keys/registries written and governing claims, never from its loops or today's counts; waste in today's output is reported and routed to the stage that owes it.
decisions.why: This is FR-001 and the design's checklist box 2 ('written from the contract alone, before the current code's numbers are read') and section 4's blind bundle. Routing a found waste to its owning stage cites the spec's Edge Cases, which the bundle does not carry (spec-cited.md omits it), but it narrows nothing.

decisions.id: D2 - a budget counts the derivation's items (items_at_40, items_at_80; budget = per_thing x items)
decisions.summary: budget-set requires the derivation's item counts at 40 and 80; make work-budget and the ratchet compute budget as per_thing x items at that size.
decisions.why: S7: 'a budget is items x candidates x checks x slack' - the items are the derivation's, not the manifest's part count. A tooling change whose only effect is that the pinned budget means what S7 says is enforcement of the request, not new scope. Mechanism defect, recorded here: D2 records items at 40 and 80 only, so it cannot produce the budget at 20 households that D5's exponent fit uses (see D5).

decisions.id: D2 legacy clause - a stage recorded before this keeps the placed-things product
decisions.summary: A budget row recorded without items keeps the old per_thing x placed-things computation; the plan asserts '(none is budgeted today)'.
decisions.why: A carve-out that preserves the very formula D2 itself calls wrong (it counts every part rather than the derivation's items and gives seat and sink a budget of 0) - the GM's S7 rule is that a budget is the derivation's items x candidates x checks x slack. None of the three grounds holds: refusing (or migrating) a row without items is trivially possible, nothing in the GM's words implies a legacy formula, and the literal rule defeats no purpose. Its reach rests on an unmeasured parenthetical: the only dated measurement in these blocks (run 20261028T152105Z-45aa176ec9b8) is cited for the placed column, not for which rows carry a budget. If it reaches nothing, deleting it costs nothing; if it reaches something, the standing record shows a non-S7 number as a budget. Fix: a row without items_at_40/items_at_80 is refused by make work-budget and the ratchet, not computed the old way.

decisions.summary: Each derivation bundled through make work-budget-bundle MODE=budget and dispatched to work-budget; LOOSE/UNDERIVED corrected and re-dispatched; a third round on one stage owes the round arbiter's ruling first; only SOUND is pinned; at most three dispatches per message.
decisions.why: FR-001 (the verdict on a bundle that passed 443 FR-008's refusal) and SC-001 (SOUND). The arbiter's ruling is on process; the plan still requires SOUND to pin, consistent with the design's 'may rule on process'. Dispatch batching is process.

decisions.id: D4 - the 23 stages in four families, one task per family
decisions.summary: Water (6), homesteads (7), ways (3), hinterland and frame (7), as 443's T09-T12 grouped them; one landing per family.
decisions.why: Grouping stages into tasks narrows nothing, and the Summary and T06 state the scope as every stage of STAGES (FR-001). Gap, not ruled: the list's search space is '443's T09-T12', not a census of STAGES; the design says 'about 25 stages' and nothing in the blocks shows 23 = len(STAGES). I could not check it (the bundle forbids the repository). The plan should state the census - STAGES itself or the run's stage rows, dated - so a stage 443 did not group cannot fall out of 'every stage'.

decisions.summary: Target = sum of the 23 budgets at 40 households and the whole roll's exponent (fit of summed budgets at 20, 40, 80); today's figures and per-stage ratios read only after every budget is pinned and sent beside it; escalation-check, then the GM; make budget-program records his words; no phase task filed before.
decisions.why: FR-002 and the design's step 3 ('The GM approves the target'). Reading today's counts only after pinning keeps FR-001's blindness. Mechanism defect, recorded here: the fit uses budgets at 20 households that D2 cannot produce (items are recorded at 40 and 80 only). The faithful fix is items_at_20; fitting from 40 and 80 alone would be narrower than S6's 20-to-80 band and would itself need a ruling.

decisions.id: Technical Context / Performance bookends / Constitution Check
decisions.summary: Step 3 changes no code a roll runs; perf bookends per phase task; figures no claim states are labeled guesses (XII).
decisions.why: Statements of fact and process consistent with the design; nothing narrowed.

decisions.summary: This plan plans step 3 (T01-T06) in full; each phase task is filed after the GM's checkpoint with its own plan section and plan review (make task-add, make plan-delta).
decisions.why: Sequencing, not scope: the request's step 3 puts the GM's approval of the target before any phase, and FR-003's one-task-per-phase is kept, only filed later. Nothing of steps 4-6 is dropped; the Summary and Project Structure still name FR-003 to FR-012.

decisions.summary: A derivation per stage from its contract alone; the CONTRACT is read from the stage's docstring, the plan fields it reads, the manifest keys and registries it writes, and the research claims that govern it - never from its loops or today's counts.
decisions.why: The design the GM approved defines the contract (checklist box 1) as four things: what the phase reads, what it writes, the governing research claims, AND 'the cohort properties it must keep'; box 2 says the algorithm is 'written from the contract alone'. D1 lists the sources of the contract and omits the cohort properties. They are not a reporting detail: under S4 and FR-004 every rule is asked of a candidate before placing, and a cohort property is a rule the output must satisfy, so it contributes checks to S7's items x candidates x checks x slack. A derivation blind to them undercounts checks, and the target the GM approves at T06 (D5) is built on that undercount - the purpose of step 3 is a target he can hold the program to. Not impossible, not implied by D1's named sources (that the docstring may state them is completing the request's thought), and including them does not defeat the request's purpose. Fix: add 'the cohort properties the stage must keep' to D1's contract sources (and to the derivation's form if the template has no place for them). The anti-anchoring rule (no loops, no counts) is within and stands.

decisions.summary: Where a derivation finds today's output wasteful (a thing placed that a later stage drops), it says so and the fix goes to the stage that owes it.
decisions.why: S4 (nothing placed then dropped) applied across stages; the spec's Edge Cases carry it. Narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A budgeted stage records items_at_20/40/80 from its derivation (1 for a whole-stage figure); its budget at a size is per_thing x items; make budget-set requires them; make work-budget and the ratchet refuse a budgeted or accepted row without them, naming make budget-change; the placed-things product is retired, not kept for older rows.
decisions.why: Makes S7's 'items x candidates x checks x slack' the literal budget, and gives the stages that place nothing (seat, sink) a real figure instead of 0. items_at_20 is what D5's 20-80 exponent fit and S6's 20-to-80 exponent need. The earlier text's carve-out (older rows keep the placed-things product) is gone: no residual path computes a budget without items, and the refusal names make budget-change rather than falling back. Changes no budget's value, so 'budgets change only with the GM's words' is untouched.

decisions.summary: Each derivation bundled with make work-budget-bundle MODE=budget and dispatched to the work-budget agent; first line saved as <stage>.verdict.txt and its row ledgered; LOOSE/UNDERIVED corrected and redispatched; a third round on one stage owes the round arbiter's ruling first; only SOUND is pinned by make budget-set; plain Agent calls, at most three per message.
decisions.why: Implements step 3's 'MODE BUDGET on each' and FR-001. SOUND remains the only route to a pinned budget, so the arbiter's ruling before a third round is a process ruling, not an acceptance of an un-SOUND budget - consistent with the request's limit on the arbiter. The dispatch mechanics are operational.

decisions.summary: Every stage of STAGES - 23, measured 2026-10-28 from driver.py's STAGES tuple - in four families (water 6, homesteads 7, ways 3, hinterland and frame 7), one task per family.
decisions.why: The request says 'about 25 stages'; the plan derives every one and now states where the 23 comes from. 6+7+3+7=23. Grouping into four tasks is task size, not scope.

decisions.summary: The target is the sum of the 23 budgets at 40 households and the whole roll's exponent from the summed budgets at 20/40/80; today's counts and ratios are read only after every budget is pinned; the draft goes through escalation-check to the GM, whose words set it with make budget-program; no phase task is filed before.
decisions.why: Step 3: 'their sum, which is the program's target. The GM approves the target.' Reading today's counts only after pinning serves 'before the current code's numbers are read'. The exponent alongside the sum serves S6 and FR-009's 40-and-80 close.

decisions.summary: A derivation figure no research claim states is labeled a guess in the derivation's reason column.
decisions.why: Governs what the session writes, not what the judge may rule: a labeled guess is still exposed to an UNDERIVED verdict under S7. Narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Step 3 takes no perf bookend (it changes no code a roll runs); each phase takes its own; the opening record is 443's run 20261028T152105Z-45aa176ec9b8.
decisions.why: Step 3 is paper budgets plus T01's tooling; the phases keep make perf-ab in box 6 as the request asks.

decisions.summary: T01 reads the placed column of today's make work-budget run to establish that seat and sink place nothing.
decisions.why: Tooling justification read from what the manifest counts, not operation counts; it informs no stage's budget and so anchors nothing.

decisions.summary: T01 D2's tooling with red-with-each-condition-deleted tests; T02-T05 each family's derivations, SOUND verdicts and budgets; T06 the checkpoint, after T02-T05 and before any phase task.
decisions.why: Each is the decision it names carried into a task; the exits and done-measured lines check the decisions rather than adding behavior.

blocks: ### T01 - a budget counts the derivation's own items (D2)

decisions.summary: items_at_20/40/80 recorded beside per_thing; make budget-set requires them; make work-budget and the ratchet read them and refuse a budgeted row without them
decisions.why: This is the spec's own D2, carried out as written: the budget at each size is per_thing x the derivation's items, which is S7's items x candidates x checks x slack (request section 2), and the placed-things product is retired. 'A budgeted row' covers D2's 'budgeted or accepted row', because a phase is accepted only against its budget. The block does not repeat D2's detail that the refusal names the row and make budget-change, and it does not narrow that detail either: the block cites D2, so D2 still governs.

decisions.summary: the budget bundle's form check also requires the contract's Reads:, Writes: and Keeps: lines (cohort properties and claims), each filled
decisions.why: This enforces the design's checklist box 1 (request section 3: what the phase reads and writes, the claims that govern it, the cohort properties it keeps) and FR-001 (each derivation written from the stage's contract alone). It refuses only a bundle that lacks the thing the GM asked for, so it reaches nothing beyond the request. It adds a check and narrows nothing. Aside, not a ruling: exit 6 gives no test and no red-with-the-check-deleted case for this form check, though it does for the items refusals.

decisions.summary: seat and sink place nothing, so they take a whole-stage figure (items = 1)
decisions.why: D2 and the spec's Edge Cases settle the whole-stage figure. The premise is MEASURED and dated (make work-budget, run 20261028T152105Z-45aa176ec9b8, its placed column), not assumed.

decisions.summary: T01 goes first because T02-T05's budget-set calls need it; one landing; exits green on tests, red recorded and an impossibility claim sent to make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: These are sequencing and process choices inside the request. None of them changes what is built or relaxes any standard. The arbiter is asked only whether the task can be done, not to accept a phase over budget, so this matches request section 5 item 4.

blocks: ### T02 - the water family's budgets (D1, D3, D4)

decisions.summary: The task covers the six water stages (water_frame, field, sink, waterward, pond_stock, pond_bank), each derived, judged SOUND and pinned, landed together.
decisions.why: D4 lists exactly these six as the water family, one task per family landing derivations, verdicts and budgets together; the request's step 3 derives every stage's budget on paper with MODE BUDGET on each. No stage of the family is left out.

decisions.summary: Goal: each budget found derived by an independent judge blind to today's code and counts.
decisions.why: FR-001 and the request's section 4 (the MODE BUDGET bundle does not hold the current code or its numbers, so today's waste cannot anchor the target). The cited D1 also keeps the counts out of the writing.

decisions.summary: Item 4: each stage's contract is read from D1's five sources - docstring, the plan fields it reads, the manifest keys and registries it writes (dev/placement.md's STAGES table and draw order), its claims (make claims-report) and the cohort's checks of what it places (cohort_audit's rules).
decisions.why: This is the changed passage. The earlier text (docstring, dev/placement.md and claims only) dropped the inputs read and the cohort properties; the new text carries all five of D1's sources, which are the request's checklist item 1 (what the phase reads from the manifest and writes, the claims that govern it, the cohort properties it must keep). It now matches D1 in full and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: After T01.
decisions.why: T01 makes a budget count the derivation's own items, which the budgets pinned here need; sequencing only, the spec leaves it open and it narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Green: six SOUND verdicts recorded and six budgets pinned. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down; a claim that it cannot be done is ruled through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The green exit is SC-001 for this family. The red exit does not let a stage go unbudgeted: a set-down task leaves the stage without a SOUND verdict, so SC-001 and FR-009 keep the feature open, and the impossibility claim goes to the arbiter, not to the session. It is not the 'set down when the gain is small' exit the request's section 5 forbids (no time saving is weighed here), and D3's correction loop and third-round tripwire are kept by citing D3.

decisions.summary: One landing; six dispatches, more where a verdict asks a correction.
decisions.why: D3: one dispatch per derivation, re-dispatched after a LOOSE or UNDERIVED correction; D4: one landing per family.

decisions.summary: Six budgeted rows in dev/work-budget.json, each with its derivation and verdict.
decisions.why: D3 saves each verdict beside its derivation, writes its ledger row and pins SOUND budgets with make budget-set; the request's standing record (section 5 item 2) is where budgets are pinned (checklist item 3).

decisions.summary: Not performance work: paper budgets, no code a roll runs changes.
decisions.why: The request's step 3 derives budgets on paper; rebuilds begin in step 4.

blocks: ### T07 - a derivation's arithmetic and its index cells checked before any dispatch (the GM 2026-10-28)

decisions.summary: T03 item 4 now names the five contract sources a derivation is written from (docstring, plan fields read, manifest keys/registries written, claims, cohort checks)
decisions.why: Word-for-word restatement of accepted D1's definition of the CONTRACT; decides nothing the spec leaves open.

decisions.summary: T04 item 4, the same five-source contract wording
decisions.why: Restates D1; no new decision.

decisions.summary: T05 item 4, the same five-source contract wording
decisions.why: Restates D1; no new decision.

decisions.summary: The derivation template gains a ## Totals section (one line per size, expression = value) that make work-budget-bundle MODE=budget evaluates, refusing a missing size or a value off its expression, before any dispatch
decisions.why: Directly answers the GM's 2026-10-28 rule that 'careful' must mean the checklist-based process is updated and enforced in tooling; a sum written wrong (19 + 8 as 26) is refused.

decisions.summary: The value may differ from its evaluated expression by up to 1% (labeled a CONVENTION for the rounding a hand-written total carries)
decisions.why: Exact equality between a hand-written rounded value and an expression with non-integer factors (slack, log terms) is physically unattainable, so some band is forced; the named slip (19 + 8 as 26, about 3.7%) still trips 1%, so the band does not gut the check's purpose.

decisions.summary: The arithmetic check refuses only a total off its own expression; the Why names 'a total leaving out a term' and 'a figure read at half its size' among the slips 'a script could have refused before any dispatch', but no refusal checks the expression's terms or figures against the count table
decisions.why: Exit 6 lists exactly three refusals: 'a missing size, a total off its expression and an indexed derivation with no cells row'. An expression that omits a count-table term, or uses a figure at half its table value, evaluates to its own written value and passes; 'the expression in the count table's own figures' is an instruction to the writer, not a stated refusal. So two of the four slip classes the block itself defines as what 'careful' meant stay with the session's care and the judge's rounds - exactly what the GM said (2026-10-28) 'will not work'. Not physically impossible (the count table is in the same file: every count row can be required as a term, every figure in the expression required to be a table cell), not implied by the GM's words, and enforcing it does not defeat the request's purpose. To clear: add refusals for an expression missing a count row's term and for a figure in the expression that is not the table's value for that size, each red with its condition deleted, or drop those two slips from the Why's claim and state how they are otherwise checked.

decisions.summary: A derivation whose 'Cheaper algorithms considered' says a grid or spatial index is used must hold a count row whose factor names the cells examined, or is refused
decisions.why: Answers the named slip (index cells left uncounted, field and sink rounds) and the rubric's S1/S5. The trigger is a self-report in one section, a seam worth widening (an index named only in the pseudocode escapes), but that section exists to answer the rubric's grid question, so the check reaches the case it names.

decisions.summary: T07 lands in 444, before T02's next dispatch, and applies to every later derivation
decisions.why: The GM, 2026-10-28: 'as long as it happens before the place where it would actually matter, then I don't care which feature it belongs to.'

blocks: ### T07 - a derivation's arithmetic and its index cells checked before any dispatch (the GM 2026-10-28)

decisions.summary: Each family's derivations written from D1's five contract sources (docstring, plan fields read, manifest keys and registries written, claims, cohort checks), never the code or today's counts
decisions.why: D1 verbatim; serves request section 3 box 2 ('written from the contract alone') and section 4 (today's waste cannot anchor the target). The three blocks are byte-identical to their BLOCKED text in earlier.md, which records no reason; read afresh, nothing in them departs from the request or the spec.

decisions.summary: After T01; one dispatch per stage, more on a LOOSE/UNDERIVED correction, the third round owing the arbiter (D3)
decisions.why: D3 and FR-001 as written; request section 6 step 3 (MODE BUDGET on each stage).

decisions.summary: Green: every stage of the family SOUND and pinned (seven / three / seven); red: task set down with a cannot-be-done claim ruled through make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: Green requires a SOUND verdict and a pin for every stage, as FR-001/SC-001 and step 3 ask. The red exit sets down the task, not the requirement: it accepts no budget and no phase over budget (request 5.4), and the feature cannot close without every stage's SOUND verdict (SC-001). The stage counts (7 + 3 + 7) carry no search space in the bundle - item 4 cites dev/placement.md's STAGES table as a source but the blocks never say the counts came from it - so I could not confirm they cover 'every stage' (the request says about 25); not shown to under-count, so not ruled a narrowing.

decisions.summary: make work-budget-bundle MODE=budget evaluates each Totals expression and refuses a value more than 1% off it (a CONVENTION for hand-written rounding)
decisions.why: The block's own goal is totals 'arithmetically true', and the slip it is for is a sum written wrong (19 + 8 as 26). A relative 1% band refuses that slip only while the total is under about 100. Request section 2 puts a stage at 2,000-4,000 ops per house, so a total at 80 households is in the hundreds of thousands, and 1% admits an error of thousands: the incident's exact slip inside such a sum passes, and so does a whole omitted row smaller than 1%. That leaves 'being careful' as the only defense below the band, which is what the GM's rule refuses. An exact check is possible (the script computes the value; compare it rounded to an integer, or let the value be the evaluator's own). Convenience in writing a rounded total is not impossibility. Fix: refuse any value that differs from its expression's evaluation (rounded to the integer).

decisions.summary: 'A total leaving out a term of the table' left to the work-budget agent rather than refused by the script, on the premise it needs the table's meaning
decisions.why: Judged apart from the wrong-size case. The block itself requires the expression to be written 'in the count table's own figures', and T07 is already editing the template, so a check that every count-table row's figure for that size appears in that size's expression (or that the table's rows carry per-size products the script sums) is syntactic and not impossible. The premise 'needs the table's meaning' is asserted, not demonstrated. Leaving this kind to the agent's questions 1 and 3 (is a factor derived, is one padded) changes nothing from the process that produced the twelve rounds, and neither question names a total missing a term: for this kind the session's answer to the GM's 'careful made a checked step' is the status quo. Fix: refuse a Totals expression that omits a count-table row at that size, red with its condition deleted, or show concretely why the table's form makes that impossible.

decisions.summary: 'A figure read at the wrong size' (the pond's radii read as halves) left to the work-budget agent's derivation questions
decisions.why: A script that checks arithmetic cannot know that a figure is the radius rather than the diameter; that takes the contract's meaning, so the rule cannot be applied mechanically here. The GM's own words name 'enforced in our subagent checks' as a valid form of enforcement, and the MODE BUDGET bundle carries the contract against which a factor's derivation is judged. One caveat for the session: the block says the pond case was 'found by the session after sink round 3' and then that the agent 'caught each in T02', which contradict each other for this example. The claim should cite the verdict in which the agent caught a wrong-size figure, or be dropped.

decisions.summary: A derivation whose 'Cheaper algorithms considered' says a grid or spatial index is used must have a count row naming the cells examined, or it is refused
decisions.why: It enforces request section 1 ('a spatial-index query, with the number of entries it examined') and S5, and it answers the measured finding (field round 3, sink round 3). Keying the trigger on that one section is a design choice, not a fidelity question.

decisions.summary: T07 lands before T02's next dispatch and applies to every derivation after it; the water family's derivations get Totals written and must pass
decisions.why: The GM: 'as long as it happens before the place where it would actually matter, then I don't care which feature it belongs to.'

decisions.summary: Green: the bundle refuses a missing size, a total off its expression, and an indexed derivation with no cells row, each red with its condition deleted; the fixtures and the water family pass
decisions.why: It carries the narrative's mechanism; the band in 'off its expression' is ruled above (T07-totals-1pct-band) and the exits change with that fix. Sources now cite sink.verdict-3, matching the narrative.

decisions.summary: make work-budget-bundle MODE=budget refuses, naming the line: a missing size; a value that differs from its expression's evaluation rounded to the integer; an expression that leaves out a count row's figure at that size; a count row with no per-size figure (form: 'N at 20, N at 40, N at 80' or one number); a derivation whose 'Cheaper algorithms considered' says it uses a grid or spatial index but has no count row whose factor names the cells examined.
decisions.why: Each refusal turns one of the observed slips (a sum written wrong, a total leaving out a term, index cells not counted) into a refusal in the tooling, which is the form of enforcement the GM named first. decisions.summary: A figure read at the wrong size or unit (a radius taken as a diameter, a record's keys counted as its points) is left to the work-budget agent: MODE BUDGET gains a fourth question asking exactly that.
decisions.why: The GM listed 'enforced in our subagent checks' as one acceptable form of enforcement. decisions.summary: Green: each refusal fires and goes red when its condition is deleted, the agent file asks the fourth question, the fixtures pass, and the water family's derivations pass once their totals are written. decisions.why: This is the spec's own D2, carried out as written: the budget at each size is per_thing x the derivation's items, which is S7's items x candidates x checks x slack (request section 2), and the placed-things product is retired. decisions.summary: the budget bundle's form check also requires the contract's Reads:, Writes: and Keeps: lines (cohort properties and claims), each filled

It refuses only a bundle that lacks the thing the GM asked for, so it reaches nothing beyond the request. It adds a check and narrows nothing. decisions.summary: Item 4: each stage's contract is read from D1's five sources - docstring, the plan fields it reads, the manifest keys and registries it writes (dev/placement.md's STAGES table and draw order), its claims (make claims-report) and the cohort's checks of what it places (cohort_audit's rules).
